newsitem.title: UK: BT at three-year high after investor briefing.
newsitem.headline: BT at three-year high after investor briefing.

text.p: Shares in British Telecommunications Plc rose to a three-year high early on Wednesday, amid reports of a further international alliance and after a briefing for investors on its planned MCI merger, dealers and analysts said.
The stock was up 9p at 451 by 0825 GMT, its highest since February 1994, in volume of 2.1 million shares.

Earlier a report in the Finacial Times said BT planned an alliance with Telefonica of Spain, giving it a foothold in several South American countries and further expanding its international activities.
A spokeswoman for BT declined comment on the report.
BT is also engaged in a round of meetings with institutional investors aimed at setting out the benefits of its MCI merger.
John Tysoe, analyst at SocGen, said 500p was a realistic short-to-medium term target for BT shares, mainly because of market enthusiasm for the potential benefits of the Concert merger with MCI.
"The Concert deal makes a lot of sense," Tysoe said. "They are definitely ahead of the field in terms of structure and in terms of product offering."
"Two years ago I don't think anyone would guess that anyone but AT&T would be the global leader but BT and MCI are carrying all before them," the SocGen analyst said.

"The management is going round talking the story and the story is really very good," said Tysoe, "You have got high growth and high yield and there is nothing else in the telecom investment universe that remotely compares."
However not all analysts were so upbeat.
"Really I think the market is getting this one wrong," said Andrew Harrington, analyst at Salomon Brothers.

"The key call on Concert is still the UK market where the company will generate 50 percent of revenues and two thirds of its profits, and I think things are going to be a lot worse than they expect over the next few years because there is going to be more competition and greater price pressure."
"The presentation they are doing is very smooth, the international aspect is great but in my view they are too complacent on the outlook for the UK market."
By 0930 BT shares were up 13-1/2p at 455-1/2 -- their highest since February 1994 -- in heavy volume of 9.9 million shares.
